title: Waldorf Astoria New York: Movie Hotel Guide
description: Waldorf Astoria New York is the Park Avenue landmark behind Scent of a Woman and Week-End at the Waldorf. Film facts and booking tips.
h1: Waldorf Astoria New York: the real hotel from Scent of a Woman
intro: Few hotels have been on screen as often as the Waldorf Astoria, the Art Deco tower on Park Avenue that has been a Manhattan landmark since 1931. After a long closure for restoration, you can book a room in the building again.
filming: The 1945 comedy-drama Week-End at the Waldorf is set among the guests and staff of the hotel and was partly filmed on location there. Decades later, Scent of a Woman (1992) sent Al Pacino's blind retired colonel and his young companion to the Waldorf for a luxurious New York weekend. Wikipedia lists many more films shot at the hotel, among them Coming to America, The Royal Tenenbaums and Serendipity.
facts: The 47-story tower was designed by Schultze and Weaver and finished in 1931.
It was the world's tallest hotel until 1957.
The original Waldorf-Astoria stood on Fifth Avenue and was torn down in 1929 to make room for the Empire State Building.
Television series such as Sex and the City and The Sopranos have also filmed at the Waldorf.
visit: The hotel closed in 2017 and has reopened after a major restoration, with 375 hotel rooms in the lower floors and private residences above. Check the booking page for current rates and room types.
